description: Composite of four bright-field transmission electron micrographs (TEM) of 0.8C steel (Fe–18Mn–10Al–0.8C), arranged as (a)–(d); each panel carries a white panel letter in the top-left corner and a black scale bar with its length printed in white in the bottom-right corner. (a) (scale bar 0.5 μm) shows a grain crossed by closely spaced, straight, parallel slip traces lying roughly parallel to one another in a lightly contrasted matrix. (b) (0.5 μm) shows a blocky region bounded by a curved dark boundary, its interior containing individual curved and tangled dislocations together with fringe-like contrast. (c) (0.2 μm, the highest magnification panel) shows alternating light and dark elongated parallel bands of sub-micron width with dense dislocation debris concentrated in the darker bands. (d) (0.5 μm) shows a grain interior filled with dense, uniformly overlapping dislocation tangles and incipient cell walls. The caption assigns (a)–(b) to true strain ε = 0.01 and (c)–(d) to ε = 0.18, making the group a deformation sequence: planar slip in austenite (γ) with limited dislocation activity in ferrite (α) at low strain, replaced at ε = 0.18 by microband formation in γ and a strongly increased dislocation density in α, i.e. the microstructural origin of the strain-hardening behaviour of the 0.8C steel. Only the scale-bar values are printed; no axes, indices or strain labels appear on the pixels.

observations.observation: The figure is a four-panel bright-field TEM plate labelled a-d, each panel with a scale bar box in the bottom-right corner and the panel letter in a white box at the top-left.
Panel (a) shows straight, closely spaced parallel planar slip traces crossing a grain; scale bar = 0.5 μm.
Panel (b) shows a blocky region delimited by a curved dark boundary with individual curved/tangled dislocations; scale bar = 0.5 μm.
Panel (c) shows alternating light and dark elongated parallel bands of sub-micron width; scale bar = 0.2 μm, the highest magnification of the four panels.
Panel (d) shows a grain interior with dense, uniformly overlapping dislocation tangles and cell-wall-like structures; scale bar = 0.5 μm.
The images carry no axes, crystallographic indices or printed strain values; the only numbers printed in the pixels are the scale-bar lengths 0.5 μm (a, b, d) and 0.2 μm (c).
The caption states the material is 0.8C steel and the modality is TEM.
The caption assigns panels (a)-(b) to true strain ε = 0.01 and panels (c)-(d) to ε = 0.18.
The caption labels (a) planar slip (γ) and (b) dislocations (α) at ε = 0.01; and (c) microbands (γ) and (d) densely populated dislocations (α) at ε = 0.18.

Citing text states that at the beginning of deformation (ε = 0.01) traces of planar slip are found in austenite (Fig. 7(a)) and that some dislocations in ferrite exhibit a typical paired superdislocation feature (Fig. 7(b)).
The paired-superdislocation feature asserted for (b) cannot be resolved or confirmed at the supplied image resolution; only individual curved dislocations are discernible.
Citing text states that at a true strain of 0.18 microbands have formed in austenite (Fig. 7(c)) while a distinct increase in dislocation density appears in ferrite (Fig. 7(d)).

Citing text interprets the dominant single slip in austenite of 0.8C steel (Fig. 7(a)) as caused by the ordered phase making dislocation multiplication difficult, contrasting with multi-slip in the austenite of 0.5C steel (Fig. 6(a)).

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM image, 0.5 μm scale bar, of a grain traversed by several closely spaced straight parallel planar slip traces running across the field; low overall dislocation contrast in the inter-trace regions. Caption identifies this as planar slip in austenite (γ) at ε = 0.01.

Bright-field TEM image, 0.5 μm scale bar, showing a blocky ferrite (α) region bounded by a curved dark boundary, with sparsely distributed curved and tangled dislocations and fringe/moiré-like contrast inside. Caption assigns it to ε = 0.01.

Bright-field TEM image at higher magnification, 0.2 μm scale bar, showing alternating light and dark elongated parallel bands (microbands) with dense dislocation debris in the dark bands. Caption identifies microbands in austenite (γ) at ε = 0.18.

Bright-field TEM image, 0.5 μm scale bar, of a grain interior densely and uniformly populated with overlapping dislocation tangles and forming cell walls, with dark boundary regions at the edges. Caption assigns it to densely populated dislocations in ferrite (α) at ε = 0.18.
